items.text: QA recognizes the full layer taxonomy: unit, interface, contract, integration, smoke, functional, regression, exception, compatibility, and browser E2E.
QA profiles distinguish `basic`, `complete`, `closure`, and `browser`, and report whether a run is partial or complete.
Human-selected layers and commands are allowed, but partial runs are explicitly marked and cannot satisfy closure unless the selected scope matches the required profile.
Non-browser features run or justify unit, interface, contract, integration, smoke, regression, exception, and compatibility coverage before closure.
Failure attribution routes gaps to implement, test-case, change/refreeze, QA rerun, or blocked admission based on evidence.
Browser features require real browser E2E evidence for function, UI, UX, compatibility, session, and state/data consistency.
Project-native E2E scripts can be discovered or selected and bound to AC/test IDs.
Browser-required scenarios without valid browser evidence block QA/release.
Browser runner registry includes Playwright, Playwright CLI, Playwright CDP, browser-use, agent-browser, attached browser, web-access, and Obscura CDP.
Listing commands, placeholder transcripts, and documentation-only pass notes cannot satisfy acceptance.
QA acceptance transactions include run ID, source commands, runner/browser identity, accepted test IDs, evidence refs, and failure attribution.
Release consumes formal QA closure only; raw runner output or support evidence cannot directly become release pass evidence.

tasks.title: FR-001 AC-001
tasks.description: Beacon must model the full QA layer taxonomy and reject unknown layer names unless explicitly mapped.

tasks.title: FR-002 AC-002
tasks.description: Beacon must support `basic`, `complete`, `closure`, and `browser` profiles with explicit completeness semantics.

tasks.title: FR-003 AC-003
tasks.description: `beacon qa run` must accept human-selected layer commands and persist command, layer, profile, partial/complete status, and evidence refs.

tasks.title: FR-004 AC-004
tasks.description: Non-browser features must run or justify all applicable non-browser layers before closure.

tasks.title: FR-005 AC-005
tasks.description: Browser features must require browser E2E plus UI/UX evidence, not only functional or backend evidence.

tasks.title: FR-006 AC-006
tasks.description: Beacon must discover or import project-native E2E scripts and bind them to AC/test IDs.

tasks.title: FR-007 AC-007
tasks.description: Beacon must expose a governed browser runner registry and record selected runner/browser identity.

tasks.title: FR-008 AC-008
tasks.description: Listing commands and placeholder evidence must be classified as non-acceptance evidence.

tasks.title: FR-009 AC-009
tasks.description: QA acceptance writeback must include run ID, source command, accepted test IDs, evidence refs, and attribution.

tasks.title: FR-010 AC-010
tasks.description: Missing or invalid browser evidence for browser-required scenarios must block QA/release.

tasks.title: FR-011 AC-011
tasks.description: Failure attribution must produce deterministic route recommendation.

tasks.title: FR-012 AC-012
tasks.description: Release readiness must consume formal QA closure, not raw support or runner output.

planner.purpose: Compile execution-ready task scope from the frozen revision baseline.

implementation-architect.purpose: Translate frozen requirement truth into implementation-safe module boundaries and service ownership guidance.

implementer.purpose: Write code inside the frozen scope and the implementation architecture note.

reviewer.purpose: Review implementation/spec drift and architecture-boundary drift.

tester.purpose: Check implementation evidence and verification readiness before acceptance.

implementation_preflight: Before implementation, verify the target service belongs to: .
Before implementation, verify the current branch is beacon/v1.4.10.
If a branch switch is needed and the worktree is dirty, stop and clean or stash first.

inputs_contract: conditionally required `prototype` when the feature has real UX/UI handoff
current gate / blocked reason / branch or execution governance context when present
decision_protocol: Enter `implement` only after requirement truth is frozen enough for execution.
Block when frozen truth requires `change`, when cutover guardrails fail, or when a conditionally triggered prototype is still missing.
Keep `implement` as the only execution entry; `ask --execute` and support surfaces may route here but must not replace it.
Prefer explanation and routing logic in skill surface; keep final schema, contract, and gate writes in Python guardrails.
When dual-read or compatibility windows exist, fail closed on mismatch.
anti_inertia_notes: `implement` is not permission to rewrite requirement truth.
`goal`, task ledgers, or partial execution progress do not define completion truth.
If the feature needs UX/UI handoff and prototype is triggered, do not skip straight into coding.
Team/runtime internals stay internal unless the user explicitly asks for them.
`implement` cannot rewrite frozen truth or override gate truth by itself.
learning_notes: Reuse implementation learning to avoid repeated blocked paths or flaky cutovers.
Learning may shape route explanation and caution, but cannot override gate truth.
Downgrade stale learning instead of silently trusting it.
backstop_cli: `beacon qa ...` after implementation evidence is ready
decision_surface.primary_reason: Enter `implement` only after requirement truth is frozen enough for execution.
